title: Our, your and their home; saját

sections.content: For “our”, “your” (several people) and “their” there are three more endings: *-nk*, *-tok/-tek* and *-uk/-ük* (or *-juk/-jük*). After a vowel: *szoba* becomes *szobánk*, *szobátok*, *szobájuk*. After a consonant the first two take a linking vowel: *lakás* becomes *lakásunk*, *lakásotok*, *lakásuk*.

sections.title: Own: saját
sections.content: *Saját* (“own”) goes before the noun and never changes. The noun carries the ending: *saját szobám* (my own room), *saját kertünk* (our own garden). *Van saját szobám* means “I have my own room”; *Nincs saját szobám* means “I do not”.

items.english: I do not have my own room.

sections.content: Keep *a szobája* (his or her room) apart from *a szobájuk* (their room). The extra *-uk* shows that more than one person owns it.
